## Proof

Let
$$S_n=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\frac{(-1)^k}{k+1}\,2^{n-k}\binom{n}{k}.$$

**Step 1: Simplify the sum.**

Use the identity $\displaystyle\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{n}{k}=\frac{1}{n+1}\binom{n+1}{k+1}$. Then

$$S_n=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-1)^k\binom{n+1}{k+1}2^{n-k}.$$

Set $j=k+1$ (so $k=j-1$, $j=1,\dots,n+1$):

$$S_n=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{j=1}^{n+1}(-1)^{j-1}\binom{n+1}{j}2^{n+1-j}=\frac{-1}{n+1}\sum_{j=1}^{n+1}(-1)^{j}\binom{n+1}{j}2^{n+1-j}.$$

By the binomial theorem,
$$\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^j\binom{n+1}{j}2^{n+1-j}=(2-1)^{n+1}=1.$$

Hence
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n+1}(-1)^j\binom{n+1}{j}2^{n+1-j}=1-\binom{n+1}{0}2^{n+1}=1-2^{n+1}.$$

Therefore
$$S_n=\frac{-1}{n+1}\bigl(1-2^{n+1}\bigr)=\frac{2^{n+1}-1}{n+1}.$$

**Step 2: Evaluate the limit.**

$$\sqrt[n]{S_n}=\left(\frac{2^{n+1}-1}{n+1}\right)^{1/n}.$$

Taking logarithms,
$$\ln\sqrt[n]{S_n}=\frac{1}{n}\ln(2^{n+1}-1)-\frac{1}{n}\ln(n+1).$$

For the first term:
$$\frac{1}{n}\ln(2^{n+1}-1)=\frac{1}{n}\Bigl[(n+1)\ln 2+\ln\!\bigl(1-2^{-(n+1)}\bigr)\Bigr]\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\ln 2+0=\ln 2.$$

For the second term:
$$\frac{1}{n}\ln(n+1)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.$$

Thus
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\ln\sqrt[n]{S_n}=\ln 2,$$

and by continuity of the exponential,

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{S_n}=e^{\ln 2}=\boxed{2}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
